50353497.DESCRIPTION: Inhibition of human recombinant wild type galectin 3 after 60 mins by surface plasmon resonance immunosensor assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 4.4. Surface pla: To evaluate in real time the interaction between galectin-3 and the different glycoconjugates, measurements were performed by the SPR technique. For the measurements, an Autolab Spirit instrument (Eco Chemie B.V., Utrecht, The Netherlands) was used. Its optical system consisted of a glass prism and a planar gold SPR disk, which were both obtained from Xantec Bioanalytics (Muenster, Germany). The equipment has a laser diode with a wavelength fixed at 670 nm. This system is equipped with a cuvette, and its operation mode is based on the Kretschmann configuration. Typically, the experiments (23 ± 1 °C) were conducted in PBS buffer solution at pH 7.4 at a flow rate of 48 μL/min. 4.4.2. Construction of the SPR immunosensors SPR substrates were cleaned in piranha solution (1:3 mixture of 30% H2O2 and concentrated H2SO4) for approximately 3–5 min, followed by the immersion of each one in acetone (5 min) and then in isopropyl alcohol (5 min). Afterward, the substrates were washed several times with deionized water and dried with a pure N2(g) flow. Then, a self-assembled monolayer (SAM) on the SPR substrates was formed by the adsorption of cysteamine (CYS) on the gold surfaces from an ethanolic solution (1.0 mmol L−1) during 24 h. The SAM/Au formed was copiously washed with ethanol and dried with a pure N2(g) flow. Subsequently, the terminal carboxyl groups of the glycoconjugates 1–6 (each solution consisting of 150 mmol L−1 of the glycoconjugate) were activated by the addition of an aqueous solution containing EDC (200 mmol L−1) and NHS (100 mmol L−1) for approximately 30 min for the formation of the NHS-ester groups. Then, each one of the previously activated glycoconjugates 1–6 was bonded on the SAM/Au during 60 min for the construction of the SPR immunosensors. The excess of unbounded molecules was removed through several additions of PBS buffer solution at pH 7.4. Afterward, the SPR sensors were dried with pure N2(g) flow. In turn, the strategy adopted for the immobilization of the glycoconjugate 7 and lactose on the SAM/Au was different. After the formation of the SAM/Au, the terminal amino groups of the CYS were activated by the addition of an aqueous solution containing glutaraldehyde (2.5%) for approximately 30 min. After, the glycoconjugate 7 (150 mmol L−1) and the lactose (150 mmol L−1) were bonded during 60 min on the previously activated SAM/Au for the construction of the SPR immunosensors. Then, for each one of the SPR sensors the unbound reactive groups were deactivated by a brief flow of 1.0 mol L−1 of an ethanolamine (EA) aqueous solution for approximately 5 min to prevent non-specific binding. The excess of unbounded EA molecules was removed through several additions of water. After this, each SPR immunosensor was dried with pure N2(g) flow. The interaction kinetics of galectin-3 towards the different glycoconjugates 1–7 and lactose was evaluated by the SPR immunosensors through the curves of association–dissociation. For these measurements, the addition of different concentrations of galectin-3 (1.90, 3.90, 11.6, 19.2, 26.9, 30.8 and 38.5 μM L−1, dissolved in PBS buffer solution at pH 7.4) on each glycoconjugate covalently immobilized on the SPR sensor discs was performed. The results of these analyses were extracted to a software of kinetics modeling (TraceDrawer, version 1.5) and both the values of the association kinetic constants (ka) and the dissociation kinetic constants (kd) were estimated. Thus, through the values of the equilibrium dissociation constant, KD (kd/ka), it was possible to evaluate the binding affinity between each glycoconjugate with galectin-3.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. Sensorgrams showing the association and dissociation steps for the addition of different concentrations of galectin-3 (3.90–38.5 μM) on the glycoconjugates 3/SAM/Au (A) and 7/SAM/Au (B).
original_paragraph.Table 1: Table 1 Equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) obtained from the SPR curves | Glycoconjugates | KD (10−6 M) | χ2 (chi2) | |---|---|---| | 1 (Thr) | 88.2 | 7.68 | | 2 (Phe) | 7.96 | 7.86 | | 3 (Trp) | 28.1 | 2.94 | | 4 (Lys) | 4.56 | 8.62 | | 5 (Asp) | 11.1 | 10.2 | | 6 (Tyr) | 19.9 | 5.20 | | 7 (Lac) | KD1 0.15/KD2 19.0 | 4.55 | | Lactose | 92.6 | 5.42 | a The deviations found for these measurements were not significant (<5%). b KD1 and KD2 refer to the first and second CRDs of galectin-3 that interact with glycoconjugate 7.
original_paragraph.Results - 2.2. Surface plasmon resonance: SPR assays were utilized for evaluation of the binding affinity between galectin-3 (recombinant human wild type) and the obtained glycoconjugates 1–7. Thus, the assessment of the interaction of galectin-3 towards the glycoconjugates 1–7 and lactose, used as control, was carried out by the addition of galectin-3 on the immunosensors containing these compounds covalently immobilized on a self-assembled monolayer (SAM/Au). The analyses were then performed in three consecutive steps, involving initial stabilization of the baseline and monitoring of the response (ΔθSPR) (~50 s), followed by addition of different concentrations of galectin-3 (1.90–38.5 μM) on each glycoconjugate (150 mM) covalently immobilized on the SPR sensor discs (10–12 min). This step constitutes the association phase associated to the binding of galectin-3 to the glycoconjugate. In the final step, comprising the dissociation phase, unbound molecules were removed from the surface of the immunosensor by successive washes with PBS buffer. The association and dissociation phases obtained by the SPR technique due to the interaction of galectin-3 with the glycoconjugate 3, which here was selected as an example among the tested amino acids-derived glycoconjugates, and the divalent lactose 7 is shown in Figure 2A and B. Based on the SPR curves (Fig. 2), it was possible to observe that in both SPR immunosensors the ΔθSPR increased in proportion to the concentration of galectin-3. This occurred because the interaction of galectin-3 with each glycoconjugate (3 and 7) increased the refractive index of the environment. In a similar way, these same conditions were applied for analysis of the others SPR immunosensors containing the glycoconjugates 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, and lactose, and the achieved results (data shown in the Supplementary information, Fig. S29) were in accordance with the ones obtained for the glycoconjugates 3 and 7 (Fig. 2A and B).
